result.summary: The pedestrian environment is a typical residential row-house street with continuous sidewalks but lacks formal crossing infrastructure. Safety is compromised by utility poles obstructing the walkway and a lack of marked crosswalks or curb ramps at the visible intersection.

hazards.name: Unmarked Intersection
hazards.description: Lack of marked crosswalks at the intersection increases risk for pedestrians crossing.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles placed in the center of the sidewalk reduce the effective width for pedestrians, especially those with mobility aids.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked cars near the intersection corner may block the view between pedestrians and approaching vehicles.
hazards.location_in_image: Street corners where cars are parked

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian space and alert drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk at the corners to reduce crossing distance and prevent parking too close to the intersection, improving sightlines.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install detectable warning surfaces and sloped ramps at the corners to ensure accessibility for all users.

result.summary: The image shows a wide, paved sidewalk in good condition adjacent to a residential building. The environment is characterized by a high chain-link fence with opaque metal panels and barred windows, creating a blank frontage that lacks natural surveillance.

hazards.name: Litter and debris
hazards.description: Small amounts of trash and weeds are present at the base of the fence, which could present minor trip hazards or indicate poor maintenance.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the base of the fence on the sidewalk

hazards.name: Lack of natural surveillance
hazards.description: The opaque metal sheets on the fence and barred windows create a blank frontage that limits visibility between the building and the street.
hazards.location_in_image: The fence line and building facade

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Planting street trees would improve the pedestrian environment, provide shade, and create a more inviting atmosphere.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Installing street lights would improve visibility and safety for pedestrians during evening hours.

interventions.title: Trash Receptacles
interventions.description: Providing bins could help reduce the accumulation of litter on the walkway.

result.summary: The street features narrow sidewalks on both sides with no buffer from the roadway, which lacks lane markings and shows significant pavement degradation. There is a complete absence of pedestrian crossing infrastructure, such as marked crosswalks or curb ramps, at the visible intersection. The residential character is defined by row houses on one side and a fenced wooded area on the other.

hazards.name: Degraded Road Surface
hazards.description: The roadway is heavily patched and cracked, creating uneven surfaces for anyone crossing.
hazards.location_in_image: Center and foreground of the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Crossings
hazards.description: There are no marked crosswalks or pedestrian warning signs at the visible intersection or mid-block.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Install continental-style marked crosswalks at the intersection to define pedestrian right-of-way.

interventions.title: Roadway Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair the cracked and patched pavement to provide a smooth, predictable surface for all users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The image depicts a residential street with a continuous concrete sidewalk and a raised curb. A large vacant lot creates a significant gap in the building frontage, while on-street parking and a large vehicle in the foreground partially obstruct sightlines.

hazards.name: Blank Frontage / Vacant Lot
hazards.description: The large vacant lot reduces natural surveillance and can make pedestrians feel less safe.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicle
hazards.description: The large pickup truck parked at the curb blocks sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the roadway.

interventions.title: Infill Development or Lot Activation
interventions.description: Developing the vacant lot or turning it into a community space to increase activity and natural surveillance.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Installing curb extensions at the nearest intersection to improve visibility and shorten crossing distances.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer
interventions.description: Adding a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic.
